_README: Reviewed source-structure -> atlas-entity mappings for the University of
Denver Visible Human release, for the cases no name-similarity matcher
can or should decide by itself.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM build/vh/*_mapping.json.
That file is a per-run artifact and build/ is gitignored. Everything
learned by reading the release once has to survive the next run, the next
subject and the next machine, so it lives here in version control and is
applied automatically by `propose`.
HOW ENTRIES ARE KEYED.
On tissue class plus normalised structure name, with the side stripped:
'cartilage|femur distal'. The class is part of the key because the
release ships both Bone_Patella and Cartilage_Patella, which normalise
identically once the class token is removed. '{side}' in an atlas_id is
filled from the mesh's own side marker, so one entry covers left and
right.
RELATIONSHIPS.
'exact'      one mesh, one atlas entity, same thing.
'part_of'    the mesh is one piece of a coarser atlas entity. Several
meshes will legitimately carry the same atlas_id.
'compartment' the mesh is a named functional compartment of an atlas
muscle. compartment_id says which, so downstream code can
attach geometry to the compartment and not just the muscle.
'split'      one mesh holds SEVERAL atlas entities inside one surface, so
no naming decision can separate them -- only geometry can.
'splitter' names the routine in engine/vh_ingest.py that does
it and 'split_parts' maps each part it returns to an entity.
A splitter is written only where the separation is measurable
AND checkable against something independent.
Every entry states why. An override is a decision, and a decision with
no recorded reason is indistinguishable from a mistake.
source: Andreassen TE, Hume DR, Hamilton LD, Walker KE, Higinbotham SE, Shelburne KB, 'Three Dimensional Lower Extremity Musculoskeletal Geometry of the Visible Human Female and Male', Scientific Data 10:34 (2023), doi:10.1038/s41597-022-01905-2. CC BY 4.0.
reviewed_against: VHM right-side and left-side Final STL sets, 63 and 65 structures

entries.note: The atlas carries the seven tarsals as one entity, whose Latin name lists them individually. The release ships each separately. This is a real many-to-one, not a failed match.
Spelled 'Calcaneous' in the release. Previously matched achilles_tendon_r at 0.90 because the Achilles is also the calcaneal tendon; tissue-class constraint now blocks that.
One of the seven tarsals.
One of the seven tarsals.
One of the three cuneiforms. Scored 0.12 against tarsals_r on names alone -- the atlas name says 'cuneiforme x3' rather than naming each.
One of the three cuneiforms.
One of the three cuneiforms.

The name is wrong and it matters. The release ships no Bone_Metatarsals: this one mesh is the whole forefoot, five metatarsals and fourteen phalanges in a single surface. Mapping it to phalanges_foot alone left metatarsals_{side} with no geometry, so every muscle attaching to a metatarsal -- tibialis anterior and posterior, both peroneals, adductor hallucis, the interossei -- was skipped by the anchor audit, and a metatarsal-base attachment misfiled under phalanges would still have passed. split_forefoot() separates the two by size and cuts the one ray the segmentation welded to its toe. The name also tied phalanges_foot against phalanges_hand exactly; that tie was correct behaviour and is broken here, not by the matcher, because this is a lower-extremity release containing no upper limb.

The release names cartilage by the bone surface it covers; the atlas names it by the joint it belongs to. No name-similarity method can bridge that -- 'femur head' and 'hip articular cartilage' share no token -- which is why all eight cartilage meshes needed a curated decision rather than a better matcher.
Named 'PelvisAcetabulum' in the release; 'pelvis' normalises to 'hip'. The acetabular and femoral head surfaces are the two halves of one atlas entity.

IMPRECISE, deliberately. This single mesh covers both the tibiofemoral condyles and the trochlear surface, and the atlas splits those between knee_articular_cartilage and patellofemoral_articular_cartilage. Assigning it to the knee entity is the closer of the two, not a clean fit. Separating them needs geometric segmentation of the mesh, not a name mapping, and is left as known work rather than papered over.

Lateral tibial plateau. Do not confuse with lateral_meniscus_r, which it scored 0.33 against -- the meniscus is fibrocartilage between the surfaces, a separate atlas entity, and is not in this release.
Medial tibial plateau. The release spells this one 'TibialMedial' while its neighbours are 'TibiaLateral' and 'TibiaDistal' -- an inconsistency in the source, not a different structure.
The retropatellar surface. Distinct from bone|patella, which is why tissue class is part of the key: both normalise to 'patella'.
Tibial plafond -- the ankle, not the knee, despite sharing the word 'tibia' with the two plateau meshes.
Talar dome. Pairs with the tibial plafond as the two halves of the ankle entity.
The atlas already models the two heads as functional compartments, so this is geometry for a compartment that exists rather than a merge that loses information.
The short head has its own innervation (common fibular) distinct from the long head (tibial), which is exactly why the compartment split matters here.
Both heads carry separately published motor endplate zones in this atlas, so keeping their geometry apart is required, not optional.
See the lateral head.

Spelled 'Illiacus' in the release. The atlas models iliopsoas as one muscle with iliacus and psoas major compartments; the release ships them as separate meshes, which matches the compartments one for one.
This compartment carries the atlas's only cadaver-dissection endplate zone (Van Campenhout et al.), so attaching its geometry correctly has direct consequences for injection targeting.

Medial tibial plateau, LEFT-side spelling. The release writes 'TibialMedial' on the right and 'TibiaMedial' on the left; both are the same structure. Keyed twice rather than normalised, because turning 'tibial' into 'tibia' globally would be a rule about a word rather than about these two files.

Long head, LEFT-side spelling: the release writes 'BicepsFemorisLong' on the right and 'BicepsFemorisLongus' on the left. Not fixed by a synonym, because 'longus' is a real anatomical word -- mapping it to 'long' would corrupt adductor longus, fibularis longus and every other longus in the atlas.
